name: Open Items
rows: Fiscal year ended June 30, 2026 · USD · Year-end audit workpapers
DRAFT FOR THE CPA · audit procedures · not an audit report · no opinion expressed

Known misstatements of FY2026 income add up to $559,962.23, 164.7% of the $340,000.00 materiality, above it even with CROSS-01. Management decides whether to record them; the CPA concludes on the statements.

26-01261 (AJ-26-0633) credits Pier 9 revenue $48,000.00, posted Saturday, August 8, 2026 at 9:41 PM after the trial balance was exported, with no support, set to reverse July 2. Revenue and account 1300 overstated. The journal entry testing’s OVR-01 asks the officers about it.
Sound Ridge Mechanical Inc.’s SRM-2604-07: $186,400.00 of June work on Pier 9, received July 9, 2026, booked in July. Job cost, payables and retainage payable short.
Pellham & Quist LLP’s 2026-0712: $23,480.00 for May 4 to June 30, 2026, unpaid and unrecorded.
June interest $28,665.00, confirmed by the bank, debited July 1, not accrued.

Brought forward from the area workpapers, each by its own id and amount: WIP-01 $103,600.00 (Work in progress: Pier 9 CO-07 revenue the signed change order does not support); AR-01 $28,600.00 (Receivables: Kestrel Point credit agreed June 18, recorded in July); SE-01 $76,935.00 (Subsequent events: Corliss settlement below the billing); SE-02 $41,250.00 (Subsequent events: Brindlewood liquidated damages, final); ACC-01 $2,892.10 (Payroll: Employer taxes on the accrued wages); FEE-01 $4,065.00 (Cash: Payroll account bank charges never recorded); FA-NET $6,635.13 (Equipment: SALE-01, CAP-01, DEP-01 and LEASE-01, net).
If UL-01 is recorded, Pier 9’s cost-to-cost revenue rises $204,835.16 (the liabilities area’s CROSS-01); the CPA settles it with the job schedule testing.
Sample pick SRM-2605-1185 ($766,537.20) has no readable invoice; page 13 of the Vellumrow print is a picture. A person keys it.
SBS-2606-1004: a $840.00 change order billed and never booked. Clearly trivial: listed, not added up.

CSC-2606-1017 is billed to Juniper Ridge Partners LLC for a survey of its own land; HCS booked it in its June 30 payables. Whose cost it is, and what it means for the related party note and the amounts due from the affiliate, is for the CPA.
The warranty reserve, $125,000.00, rests on the Controller’s job-by-job schedule; the accruals schedule still gives 1% of completed contracts ($810,300.00). The CPA judges the estimate.
26-01259, the depreciation true-up, was approved by the Controller who prepared it.
The equipment audit’s lease liabilities, $2,100,383.96, are not on the balance sheet; the crane rental found in stage 3 is one of them.
Materiality is proposed at $340,000.00, 0.5% of revenue. The engagement partner sets it.
These are draft workpapers and a draft findings memo for the engagement partner. They are not an audit report and give no opinion. Nothing has been posted, signed or sent.
